claim: Checkpoint blockade immunotherapy (CBT) can induce control of cancer growth, with a fraction of patients experiencing durable responses.
source: Cancer immunotherapies, in particular checkpoint blockade immunotherapy (CBT), can induce control of cancer growth, with a fraction of patients experiencing durable responses.
evidence: This is a general statement about CBT outcomes that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The majority of patients currently do not respond to CBT.
source: However, the majority of patients currently do not respond to CBT and the molecular determinants of resistance have not been fully elucidated.
evidence: This statement reflects established clinical knowledge about CBT response rates.

claim: High intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), where the majority of NeoAgs are expressed subclonally, is correlated with poor clinical response to CBT.
source: High intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), where the majority of NeoAgs are expressed subclonally, is correlated with poor clinical response to CBT and poor infiltration with tumor-reactive T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by mounting clinical evidence mentioned in the text.

claim: High intratumor heterogeneity is correlated with poor infiltration with tumor-reactive T cells.
source: High intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), where the majority of NeoAgs are expressed subclonally, is correlated with poor clinical response to CBT and poor infiltration with tumor-reactive T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by mounting clinical evidence mentioned in the text.

claim: Clonal expression of a weakly immunogenic NeoAg with a relatively strong NeoAg increased the immunogenicity of tumors with low but not high ITH.
source: Here we show that clonal expression of a weakly immunogenic NeoAg with a relatively strong NeoAg increased the immunogenicity of tumors with low but not high ITH.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: Clonal NeoAg expression allowed cross-presenting dendritic cells to acquire and present both NeoAgs.
source: Mechanistically we determined that clonal NeoAg expression allowed cross-presenting dendritic cells to acquire and present both NeoAgs.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: Dual NeoAg presentation by dendritic cells was associated with a more mature DC phenotype.
source: Dual NeoAg presentation by dendritic cells was associated with a more mature DC phenotype and a higher stimulatory capacity.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's experimental data on DC phenotype.

claim: Dual NeoAg presentation by dendritic cells was associated with a higher stimulatory capacity.
source: Dual NeoAg presentation by dendritic cells was associated with a more mature DC phenotype and a higher stimulatory capacity.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's experimental data on DC function.

claim: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells recognize peptides on class I major histocompatibility complexes (MHCI) expressed on tumor cells.
source: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells recognize peptides on class I major histocompatibility complexes (MHCI) expressed on tumor cells, and following recognition mediate specific lysis of their target cell (Stinchcombe et al., 2001; Isaaz et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CD8+ T cells mediate specific lysis of their target cell following recognition of peptides on MHCI.
source: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells recognize peptides on class I major histocompatibility complexes (MHCI) expressed on tumor cells, and following recognition mediate specific lysis of their target cell (Stinchcombe et al., 2001; Isaaz et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Peptides specific to tumor cells are best suited to drive the most powerful anti-tumor responses.
source: While CD8+ T cells can recognize many tumor-associated antigens, peptides specific to tumor cells are best suited to drive the most powerful anti-tumor responses (Schietinger et al., 2008; Minati et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NeoAgs are predominantly derived from non-synonymous mutations in highly expressed protein coding transcripts within the tumor cells.
source: NeoAgs are predominantly derived from non-synonymous mutations in highly expressed protein coding transcripts within the tumor cells (Schumacher et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Patients responding to checkpoint blockade immunotherapy often experience an expansion in NeoAg-reactive T cells within tumor-infiltrating T cells.
source: It has been shown that patients responding to checkpoint blockade immunotherapy (CBT) often experience an expansion in NeoAg-reactive T cells within tumor-infiltrating T cells, as well as in circulation (van Rooij et al., 2013; Riaz et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: Patients responding to checkpoint blockade immunotherapy often experience an expansion in NeoAg-reactive T cells in circulation.
source: It has been shown that patients responding to checkpoint blockade immunotherapy (CBT) often experience an expansion in NeoAg-reactive T cells within tumor-infiltrating T cells, as well as in circulation (van Rooij et al., 2013; Riaz et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: Adoptive cell transfer of NeoAg-specific T cells may be beneficial.
source: Further, adoptive cell transfer of NeoAg-specific T cells may be beneficial (Robbins et al., 2013; Verdegaal et al., 2016; Gros et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: Vaccination can induce objective responses toward tumor-specific NeoAgs.
source: and vaccination can induce objective responses toward tumor-specific NeoAgs (Carreno et al., 2015; Keskin et al., 2019; Johanns et al., 2019; Ott et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: The presence of CD8+ T cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME) is established as a positive prognostic marker of response to CBT.
source: The presence of CD8+ T cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME) is established as a positive prognostic marker of response to CBT and overall survival (van der Leun et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The presence of CD8+ T cells within the tumor microenvironment is established as a positive prognostic marker of overall survival.
source: The presence of CD8+ T cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME) is established as a positive prognostic marker of response to CBT and overall survival (van der Leun et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Increased NeoAg burden is positively associated with T cell infiltration in some cancers.
source: Over the past years, many studies have aimed to establish a correlation between the presence of NeoAgs and CD8+ T cells within the tumor resulting in findings that increased NeoAg burden is positively associated with T cell infiltration in some cancers (Rooney et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: NeoAg load alone cannot predict response to CBT.
source: Despite enormous efforts, several independent reports suggest that NeoAg load alone cannot predict response to CBT (Mauriello et al., 2019; McGrail et al., 2021; Samstein et al., 2019; Ghorani et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple independent reports.

claim: The prognostic value of NeoAg burden depends on the baseline presence of a T cell infiltrate.
source: Of note, it seems the prognostic value of NeoAg burden depends on the baseline presence of a T cell infiltrate (Mauriello et al., 2019; McGrail et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In cancer types with high mutational burden, a sizable proportion of patients lack a productive T cell infiltrate, despite an abundance in predicted NeoAgs.
source: This can be best illustrated in cancer types with high mutational burden, such as melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and colon cancer. In those cancer types, a sizable proportion of patients lack a productive T cell infiltrate, despite an abundance in predicted NeoAgs (Mauriello et al., 2019; McGrail et al., 2021; Spranger et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior clinical studies.

claim: Alterations in tumor cell-intrinsic signaling pathways can mediate poor T cell infiltration.
source: Past studies have indicated that alterations in tumor cell-intrinsic signaling pathways can mediate poor T cell infiltration, typically by means of poor T cell activation or poor T cell recruitment into the TME (Nguyen and Spranger, 2020; Lawson et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Clonal NeoAg expression is associated with response to anti-PD-1 CBT in a cohort of patients with NSCLC.
source: Clinical data suggest that clonal NeoAg expression is associated with response to anti-PD-1 CBT in a cohort of patients with NSCLC and with significantly increased overall survival in melanoma patients, following treatment with anti-CTLA-4 antibodies (McGranahan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to clinical data.

claim: Clonal NeoAg expression is associated with significantly increased overall survival in melanoma patients following treatment with anti-CTLA-4 antibodies.
source: Clinical data suggest that clonal NeoAg expression is associated with response to anti-PD-1 CBT in a cohort of patients with NSCLC and with significantly increased overall survival in melanoma patients, following treatment with anti-CTLA-4 antibodies (McGranahan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to clinical data.

claim: Subclonal NeoAg expression in tumors with high ITH was found to be associated with poor CBT responses.
source: In contrast, subclonal NeoAg expression in tumors with high ITH was found to be associated with poor CBT responses and poor CD8+ T cell infiltration.
evidence: This claim is supported by clinical observations mentioned in the text.

claim: Subclonal NeoAg expression in tumors with high ITH was found to be associated with poor CD8+ T cell infiltration.
source: In contrast, subclonal NeoAg expression in tumors with high ITH was found to be associated with poor CBT responses and poor CD8+ T cell infiltration.
evidence: This claim is supported by clinical observations mentioned in the text.

claim: Immunization with the mutant Adpgk peptide induced appreciable expansion of NeoAg-specific T cells.
source: Immunization with the mutant Adpgk peptide induced appreciable expansion of NeoAg-specific T cells while immunization with Cpne1 and Aatf peptides resulted in low or non-detectable T cell responses, respectively (Figure 1A and Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Immunization with Cpne1 peptide resulted in low T cell responses.
source: Immunization with the mutant Adpgk peptide induced appreciable expansion of NeoAg-specific T cells while immunization with Cpne1 and Aatf peptides resulted in low or non-detectable T cell responses, respectively (Figure 1A and Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Immunization with Aatf peptide resulted in non-detectable T cell responses.
source: Immunization with the mutant Adpgk peptide induced appreciable expansion of NeoAg-specific T cells while immunization with Cpne1 and Aatf peptides resulted in low or non-detectable T cell responses, respectively (Figure 1A and Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: KPAdpgk exhibited early tumor control before growing out.
source: Subcutaneous implantation of the subclones expressing a single NeoAg (KPAdpgk, KPAatf, KPCpne1) indicated that KPAdpgk exhibited early tumor control before growing out while KPAatf and KPCpne1 cell lines grew out progressively (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: KPAatf cell lines grew out progressively.
source: Subcutaneous implantation of the subclones expressing a single NeoAg (KPAdpgk, KPAatf, KPCpne1) indicated that KPAdpgk exhibited early tumor control before growing out while KPAatf and KPCpne1 cell lines grew out progressively (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: KPCpne1 cell lines grew out progressively.
source: Subcutaneous implantation of the subclones expressing a single NeoAg (KPAdpgk, KPAatf, KPCpne1) indicated that KPAdpgk exhibited early tumor control before growing out while KPAatf and KPCpne1 cell lines grew out progressively (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All three cell lines grew progressively with similar kinetics in Rag2-/- mice.
source: To confirm that the initial control observed against KPAdpgk tumor cells was mediated by an adaptive immune response, we implanted all cell lines into Rag2-/- mice and observed that all three cell lines grew progressively with similar kinetics (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: KPAdpgk tumors had a greater degree of infiltration with CD8+ T cells compared to KPAatf tumors.
source: Analysis of tumor-infiltrating T cells in KPAdpgk and KPAatf showed that KPAdpgk tumors had a greater degree of infiltration with CD8+ T cells compared to KPAatf tumors (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: CD8+ T cells in KPAdpgk tumors were more activated based on CD44 staining.
source: Further, CD8+ T cells in KPAdpgk tumors were more activated based on CD44 staining (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: IFNγ ELISpot showed a greater peripheral expansion of NeoAg-specific T cells in mice implanted with KPAdpgk tumors compared to KPAatf or KPCpne1 tumors.
source: Additionally, IFNγ ELISpot showed a greater peripheral expansion of NeoAg-specific T cells in mice implanted with KPAdpgk tumors compared to KPAatf or KPCpne1 tumors (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Cpne1-expressing tumor cells were not highly immunogenic as neither CD8+ T cell infiltration nor activation were significantly different between KPCpne1 and KPmCherry tumors.
source: Assessing the T cell infiltrate in KPCpne1 and KPmCherry tumors revealed that Cpne1-expressing tumor cells were not highly immunogenic as neither CD8+ T cell infiltration nor activation were significantly different between both tumors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: The mutant Adpgk peptide was predicted to have an IC50 of 4.29 nM.
source: The immune responses observed corresponded with MHCI binding affinities predicted by NetMHC 4.0 (Nielsen et al., 2003; Andreatta and Nielsen, 2016), with the mutant Adpgk peptide predicted to have an IC50 of 4.29 nM while the other mutant peptides had IC50 values ranging from 90.16 nM (Aatf) to 182.34 nM (Cpne1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational prediction data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The mutant Aatf peptide had an IC50 value of 90.16 nM.
source: The immune responses observed corresponded with MHCI binding affinities predicted by NetMHC 4.0 (Nielsen et al., 2003; Andreatta and Nielsen, 2016), with the mutant Adpgk peptide predicted to have an IC50 of 4.29 nM while the other mutant peptides had IC50 values ranging from 90.16 nM (Aatf) to 182.34 nM (Cpne1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational prediction data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The mutant Cpne1 peptide had an IC50 value of 182.34 nM.
source: The immune responses observed corresponded with MHCI binding affinities predicted by NetMHC 4.0 (Nielsen et al., 2003; Andreatta and Nielsen, 2016), with the mutant Adpgk peptide predicted to have an IC50 of 4.29 nM while the other mutant peptides had IC50 values ranging from 90.16 nM (Aatf) to 182.34 nM (Cpne1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational prediction data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: KP-HetLow tumors exhibited drastically increased control of tumor outgrowth compared to single antigen-expressing tumors.
source: We implanted 1 × 106 cells of KP-HetHigh and KP-HetLow tumors into mice and observed drastically increased control of tumor outgrowth of KP-HetLow tumors compared to single antigen-expressing tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from tumor growth studies.

claim: KP-HetHigh grew progressively, with similar kinetics as observed for KPAatf.
source: In contrast, KP-HetHigh grew progressively, with similar kinetics as observed for KPAatf (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Quantitative PCR analysis of KP-HetHigh tumors showed progressive outgrowth of the KPAatf subclone that completely dominated the tumor by day 14 post-implantation.
source: In fact, quantitative PCR analysis of KP-HetHigh tumors showed progressive outgrowth of the KPAatf subclone that completely dominated the tumor by day 14 post-implantation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The control of KP-HetLow tumors was completely lost in Rag2-/- mice.
source: The control of KP-HetLow tumors was completely lost in Rag2-/- mice (Figure 2B), indicating that tumor control was mediated by an adaptive immune response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The change in tumor cell composition of KP-HetHigh tumors at later timepoints observed in wildtype mice was absent in Rag2-/- mutants.
source: We also found that the change in tumor cell composition of KP-HetHigh tumors at later timepoints observed in wildtype mice was also absent in Rag2-/- mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing wildtype and Rag2-/- mice.

claim: In Rag2-/- mice, KPAatf and KPAdpgk cells were maintained at nearly a 1:1 ratio.
source: Instead, KPAatf and KPAdpgk cells were maintained at nearly a 1:1 ratio (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), providing evidence for immunoediting in this model.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The T cell response toward Adpgk was significantly greater in KP-HetLow tumors compared to KP-HetHigh tumors at day 7.
source: The T cell response toward Adpgk was significantly greater in KP-HetLow tumors compared to KP-HetHigh tumors at day 7 and greater than both KP-HetHigh and KPAdpgk tumors at day 10 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental ELISpot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The T cell response toward Adpgk was greater in KP-HetLow tumors than both KP-HetHigh and KPAdpgk tumors at day 10.
source: The T cell response toward Adpgk was significantly greater in KP-HetLow tumors compared to KP-HetHigh tumors at day 7 and greater than both KP-HetHigh and KPAdpgk tumors at day 10 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental ELISpot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At days 7 and 10, the T cell response against Aatf was only detectable in mice implanted with KP-HetLow tumors and was absent in mice bearing KP-HetHigh or KPAatf tumors.
source: Strikingly, at days 7 and 10, the T cell response against Aatf was only detectable in mice implanted with KP-HetLow tumors and was absent in mice bearing KP-HetHigh or KPAatf tumors (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental ELISpot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At day 14, the Aatf and Adpgk responses were similar in all tested conditions.
source: At day 14, the Aatf and Adpgk responses were similar in all tested conditions, suggesting mixed effects of tumor size, antigen availability, and loss of functional capacity of T cells over time (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental ELISpot data shown in Figure 2B–D.

claim: Adoptively transferred CD8+ T cells from KP-HetLow-bearing donor mice slowed the growth of KPAdpgk in Rag2-/- mice.
source: Adoptively transferred CD8+ T cells from KP-HetLow-bearing donor mice slowed the growth of KPAdpgk as well as KPAatf in Rag2-/- mice (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental adoptive transfer data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Adoptively transferred CD8+ T cells from KP-HetLow-bearing donor mice slowed the growth of KPAatf in Rag2-/- mice.
source: Adoptively transferred CD8+ T cells from KP-HetLow-bearing donor mice slowed the growth of KPAdpgk as well as KPAatf in Rag2-/- mice (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental adoptive transfer data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Transfer of CD8+ T cells from KP-HetHigh-bearing donor mice resulted in improved control of KPAdpgk, but not of KPAatf.
source: In line with the weaker IFNγ ELISpot responses observed in KP-HetHigh tumors, transfer of CD8+ T cells from KP-HetHigh-bearing donor mice was less beneficial, resulting in improved control of KPAdpgk, but not of KPAatf.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental adoptive transfer data.

claim: KP-HetLow tumor cells implanted in Batf3-/- mice lost tumor control.
source: We implanted KP-HetLow tumor cells in wildtype, Rag2-/- and Batf3-/- mice, and observed a loss of tumor control in Rag2-/- and Batf3-/- mice (Figure 3A), indicating that cDC1 are required for the induction of effective T cell responses.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: cDC1 are required for the induction of effective T cell responses in KP-HetLow tumors.
source: We implanted KP-HetLow tumor cells in wildtype, Rag2-/- and Batf3-/- mice, and observed a loss of tumor control in Rag2-/- and Batf3-/- mice (Figure 3A), indicating that cDC1 are required for the induction of effective T cell responses.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the loss of tumor control in Batf3-/- mice.

claim: No significant difference in absolute numbers of cDC1 was found between KP-HetLow and KP-HetHigh tumors.
source: However, while we observed dynamic changes in the absolute numbers of cDC1 over time, no significant difference was found between the two tumor conditions (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Similar frequencies of mCherry+ cDC1 were detected in the TdLN between KP-HetLow and KP-HetHigh conditions.
source: Assessing the number of tumor cell debris carrying mCherry+ cDC1 in the TdLN further affirmed that the differences in T cell activation were not driven by a lack of migratory cDC1 bringing antigen to the TdLN as similar frequencies were detected between the two tumor conditions (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Analysis of the mCherry MFI amongst the mCherry+ cDC1 showed no significant difference between the KP-HetLow and KP-HetHigh conditions.
source: Analysis of the mCherry MFI amongst the mCherry+ cDC1 similarly showed no significant difference between the KP-HetLow and KP-HetHigh conditions (Figure 3D), suggesting that neither cDC1 recruitment to the tumor, trafficking to the TdLN, nor amount of available antigen can explain the observed differences in T cell activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The Aatf-specific T cell response was dependent on the context of the NeoAg expression patterns, with greater expansion of Aatf-specific T cells in response to KP-HetLow tumor debris compared to either KPAatf or KP-HetHigh tumor debris.
source: Consistent with our previous observations, we observed that the Aatf-specific T cell response was dependent on the context of the NeoAg expression patterns, with greater expansion of Aatf-specific T cells in response to KP-HetLow tumor debris compared to either KPAatf or KP-HetHigh tumor debris (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from irradiated cell vaccination shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Mice injected with irradiated KP-HetHigh tumor cells exhibited a significantly reduced expansion of Adpgk-specific T cells in the periphery compared to KPAdpgk and KP-HetLow.
source: In contrast, we did observe that the Adpgk response was sensitive to lower antigen availability as mice injected with irradiated KP-HetHigh tumor cells, where only 50% of the cells express Adpgk, also exhibited a significantly reduced expansion of Adpgk-specific T cells in the periphery compared to KPAdpgk and KP-HetLow, both tumors where all the cells express Adpgk (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from irradiated cell vaccination shown in Figure 3G.

claim: In KP-HetHigh tumors most of the cDC1 carrying detectable debris were either mCherry+ or ZsGreen+.
source: We first determined the proportion of single-fluorophore or double-fluorophore positive cDC1 in the TdLN at day 7 post tumor implantation and found that in KP-HetHigh tumors most of the cDC1 carrying detectable debris were either mCherry+ or ZsGreen+ (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Most tumor cell debris-positive cDC1 found in the TdLN-draining KP-HetLow tumors were double positive for both mCherry and ZsGreen.
source: In stark contrast, most tumor cell debris-positive cDC1 found in the TdLN-draining KP-HetLow tumors were double positive for both mCherry and ZsGreen (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Within the single positive cDC1 subset in both tumors, there was a bias toward ZsGreen+ cells.
source: Within the single positive cDC1 subset in both tumors, there was a bias toward ZsGreen+ cells (Figure 4C), which could be attributed to the stability of this fluorescent protein (Yi et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Double-positive cDC1 expressed significantly greater levels of CD40 compared to mCherry+ cDC1.
source: Affirming our initial hypothesis, we observed significantly greater expression of the costimulatory molecules CD40 and CD80 in double-positive cDC1 compared to mCherry+ cDC1 that engulf only Aatf-containing debris (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Double-positive cDC1 expressed significantly greater levels of CD80 compared to mCherry+ cDC1.
source: Affirming our initial hypothesis, we observed significantly greater expression of the costimulatory molecules CD40 and CD80 in double-positive cDC1 compared to mCherry+ cDC1 that engulf only Aatf-containing debris (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: CD40 expression was comparable between Adpgk-ZsGreen+ and double-positive cDC1.
source: CD40 expression was comparable between Adpgk-ZsGreen+ and double-positive cDC1, while CD80 was highly expressed on both these cDC1 populations (Figure 4D and E), suggesting that the Adpgk-specific T cell response might induce upregulation of co-stimulatory molecules.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CD80 was highly expressed on both Adpgk-ZsGreen+ and double-positive cDC1 populations.
source: CD40 expression was comparable between Adpgk-ZsGreen+ and double-positive cDC1, while CD80 was highly expressed on both these cDC1 populations (Figure 4D and E), suggesting that the Adpgk-specific T cell response might induce upregulation of co-stimulatory molecules.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: KP-HetLow tumors could be fully controlled following dual CBT therapy.
source: Consistent with clinical observations, our model showed that KP-HetLow tumors could be fully controlled following therapy (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: KP-HetHigh tumors showed mixed responses to dual CBT therapy.
source: In contrast, KP-HetHigh tumors, engineered to resemble tumor with high ITH, showed mixed responses (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Prophylactic vaccination with replicons induced a detectable Aatf-specific response 7 d post boost.
source: Using this strategy, we induced a detectable Aatf-specific response 7 d post boost (Figure 5B), unlike short peptide vaccinations (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental ELISpot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Prophylactic vaccination alone resulted in a modest reduction of tumor growth.
source: Prophylactic vaccination alone only resulted in a modest reduction of tumor growth (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The combination treatment of prophylactic vaccination and dual CBT resulted in two out of seven (29%) objective responses with one complete response and one stable disease.
source: However, we observed a synergistic effect of the combination treatment of prophylactic vaccination and dual CBT, with two out of seven (29%) objective responses with one complete response and one stable disease (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The triple combination of CBT with therapeutic vaccination and a single dose of agonistic CD40 antibody induced complete tumor control in three of five (60%) mice.
source: In stark contrast, the triple combination of CBT with therapeutic vaccination and a single dose of agonistic CD40 antibody induced complete tumor control in three of five (60%) mice and a significant delay in tumor growth in the remaining 40% of mice (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: CD40 agonism with vaccination induced a modest reduction of tumor growth with 1/5 (20%) mice exhibiting complete tumor regression.
source: CD40 agonism with vaccination was able to induce a modest reduction of tumor growth with 1/5 (20%) mice exhibiting complete tumor regression, while CD40 agonism with CBT exhibited mixed response comparable to CBT alone where stable disease was observed in 1/7 (14%) of mice although all tumors eventually progressed (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: CD40 agonism with CBT exhibited mixed response comparable to CBT alone where stable disease was observed in 1/7 (14%) of mice although all tumors eventually progressed.
source: CD40 agonism with vaccination was able to induce a modest reduction of tumor growth with 1/5 (20%) mice exhibiting complete tumor regression, while CD40 agonism with CBT exhibited mixed response comparable to CBT alone where stable disease was observed in 1/7 (14%) of mice although all tumors eventually progressed (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental therapy data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Subclonal expression of NeoAgs resulted in presentation of peptides on distinct populations of cross-presenting cDC1.
source: Mechanistically, we identified that subclonal expression of NeoAgs resulted in presentation of peptides on distinct populations of cross-presenting cDC1, which showed lower expression of costimulatory molecules such as CD40, if presenting only a peptide with a low-binding affinity.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: cDC1 presenting only a peptide with a low-binding affinity showed lower expression of costimulatory molecules such as CD40.
source: Mechanistically, we identified that subclonal expression of NeoAgs resulted in presentation of peptides on distinct populations of cross-presenting cDC1, which showed lower expression of costimulatory molecules such as CD40, if presenting only a peptide with a low-binding affinity.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: Therapeutic vaccination against weak NeoAgs demonstrated synergy with CBT only when the first dose was administered along with an anti-CD40 agonist antibody.
source: Therapeutic vaccination against weak NeoAgs demonstrated synergy with CBT only when the first dose was administered along with an anti-CD40 agonist antibody.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's therapeutic experiments.

claim: cDC1 carrying both antigens showed higher expression levels of the co-stimulatory ligands CD40 and CD80 compared to cDC1 carrying only the weak NeoAg.
source: These cDC1 showed higher expression levels of the co-stimulatory ligands CD40 and CD80 compared to cDC1 carrying only the weak NeoAg.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CD40 expression alone on cDC1 results in a more robust expansion of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: Further, it was shown that CD40 expression alone on cDC1 results in a more robust expansion of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells, further evidence that increased expression of CD40 might directly impact priming of tumor-reactive T cells (Ferris et al., 2020a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The more immunogenic Adpgk NeoAg response was dependent on the NeoAg load.
